name: m4-runtime-reflection-cha
description: Is the Leyden cache's +6% instructions a production hazard? A cached fork has `scala.reflect.runtime`'s `SynchronizedSymbol` linked from startup (it overrides `Symbol.getFlag` and `validTo`), which costs C2 its class-hierarchy inlining of those accessors (scala `LEYDEN.md`, "Where the cost is").

`cold-reflect` has no cache: the harness initialises `scala.reflect.runtime.universe` and completes a class through it before compiling, as a macro or plugin using runtime reflection would. If it matches `aot-noreplay` in instructions, any compile that touches runtime reflection pays the cost. Build `1e85ab8eba`, stock JDK 26 integration build, m4.

variantDescriptions.cold-reflect: no cache; runtime reflection touched in setup (`-Dcompilerlab.touchRuntimeReflection`)
